note: Hand-written ground truth for the 22 sample cases, read off technician_notes and resolution_text only. Written to be argued with: the `why` field on the awkward cases is the claim, and a reviewer who disagrees with one should change this file rather than the code. In production this file is the output of a service engineer labelling a stratified sample of a few hundred cases, and it is regenerated whenever the taxonomy version changes.

labels.why: German wording of C-48211. Same cause id or the corpus splits by language.
Fixed with a torque wrench and no part. parts_replaced is empty and the case is fully diagnosed.
Customer said oil, technician found condensate. The cause is the technician's; the customer's wording is a mismatch flag, not a second opinion.
Continuous leak under load with a scored bore. Same component as C-48604, different cause, different part.
Sealant, kit on order, resolution_text null. The diagnosis is probably right and was never verified.
Screen cleaned, no part. Also the corpus's clearest example of an explicit absence of error codes.
The symptom is a flat battery and the cause is the alternator. The obvious label is the wrong one.
Nearly the same symptom as C-49002 with the opposite cause. The pair is the argument for asking about charging voltage.
Whole unit swapped under warranty, never stripped. parts_replaced lists UNIT-CX450 and the case still has no root cause.
Italian wording of C-48899, including E207 written without the hyphen.
Intermittent cold-start fault that did not reproduce. The fault is real; this visit found nothing.
Knocking like C-49402 but the cause is a broken reed, not a bearing. Also the only CX-300 in the corpus, so retrieval has to back off to the family.
Cold side, slow drip, corroded fitting. C-49511 is hot side, spraying, pump seal. Side and severity are what separate them.
Description is three words with no side and no severity. The right answer here is a low-confidence spread, not a confident pump seal.
